kept.heading: HOW GEN Z KILLED MILLENNIAL MINIMALISM (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Packaging is splitting from the clean, muted, Instagram-minimal look that defined brands like Glossier and Warby Parker toward louder colors, illustration, and visible imperfection. The shift shows up across categories that once signaled seriousness through restraint: soda alternatives adopting soda-bright packaging, wellness brands trading polish for handmade textures, and hand sanitizer redesigned as a beauty accessory worth carrying. The change isn't really about killing minimalism - it's about killing sameness, since the muted aesthetic stopped differentiating once every brand copied it.

kept.heading: HOW MUCH OF THE INTERNET IS WRITTEN WITH AI? (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: About 10% of webpages now show significant signs of AI authorship, rising to more than one-third of pages published since ChatGPT launched. AI-written content is also becoming easier to spot, with phrases, vocabulary, and punctuation associated with AI appearing more often across the web. The trend is strongest on .com sites, where AI authorship appears roughly 2X as often as on .org and 10X more than on .edu and .gov sites.

kept.heading: HOW TEXTNOW LEARNED WHEN YOUTUBE AWARENESS STARTS DRIVING LOWER-FUNNEL LIFT (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: TextNow's 26-week YouTube experiment showed that awareness media can produce lower-funnel gains, but those gains may take months to appear. The first five weeks showed almost no cumulative lift, and 87% of the measured effect accumulated after the first two months. The campaign ended with a 1.99% Total W2PU lift, while including the six-week post-treatment window improved measured efficiency by about 8% and produced a 1.84% lift at an indexed CPIA of 98 versus a planning target of 100. The results gave TextNow a timeline for evaluating YouTube and other awareness campaigns against business outcomes instead of judging them on the short measurement cycles used for performance media.

kept.heading: HOW TO BUILD AN INEVITABLE BRAND IN 2026: A GUIDE TO MODERN BRAND STRATEGY (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: An inevitable brand starts by uncovering its core truth and emotional identity rather than relying on functional differentiation or visual design alone. The article frames brands across three levels: functional, experiential, and transformational, with the strongest brands shaping how customers see themselves. Emotional positioning builds stronger memory than repetition alone, so brands should identify the peak emotional experience they want customers to associate with the product and express it consistently. Brand leaders should then define a functional brand promise, translate its emotion into a slogan and cohesive visual system, and actively protect that system across every customer touchpoint. AI can help generate and refine brand language, but human judgment must define the underlying truth and emotion first.

kept.heading: REDDIT IS THE KEYWORD RESEARCH TOOL YOU'RE PROBABLY NOT USING (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reddit can function as a keyword research dataset that reveals content gaps based on queries Google already considers valuable. Semrush data shows Reddit ranks for roughly 166 million keywords, including 65 million on page one, and it is cited in more than 15 million AI Overview queries. You can analyze Reddit's non-brand, AI Overview, branded, and Keyword Gap rankings to identify pages that need optimization, topics that warrant new content, and customer questions that belong in FAQs or support content. The goal is not to participate on Reddit, but to use its search footprint as intelligence for building a more complete content roadmap.

kept.heading: HOW TO BUILD AI AGENTS FOR CREATIVE CAMPAIGNS (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: In this webinar, Tahnee Perry will walk through a system that takes you from a blank page to a finished campaign asset without the seven different conversations, four file exports, and twenty minutes of rewriting at the end. She'll show how to configure Cowork as your campaign agent, build three Skills every marketer and creative needs, and turn research into creative strategy. The free webinar will take place on September 3 at 3:00 PM PT.

kept.heading: SHALLOW INTENT: WHY PEOPLE DON'T LIKE AI CONTENT, AND HOW TO MAKE IT GREAT (16 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI content decouples two things that used to move together: how polished something looks and how much thought went into it. Models recombine statistical patterns from everything they've seen rather than reasoning through each choice, so the result can look intricate while containing contradictions a human creator would never make, mismatched historical details, textures that ghost and repeat. People have learned to read aesthetic density as a signal of intent, so shallow intent behind a dense surface feels like a betrayal. The solution isn't necessarily less AI - it's a deliberate human pass that adds the missing depth before shipping.

kept.heading: REDDIT'S CITATIONS IN CHATGPT FALL FROM 3.8% TO 0.5% (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The collapse coincided with a change to how ChatGPT fans out search queries on August 8.

kept.heading: SONY MUSIC, WARNER SUE ANTHROPIC, ALLEGING INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY THEFT (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic is being sued for allegedly downloading and scraping copyrighted books, lyrics, and sheet music to train Claude. The case follows a $1.5B settlement with authors over similar claims of using pirated training data.

kept.heading: MARKETING CAREERS AREN'T JUST ‘POSTING ON INSTAGRAM.' WOMEN IN SPAM WANT MORE RESPECT (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Marketing is often described in casual terms that diminish the profession. Laura Cameron created “Women in SPAM” (Social Media, Public Relations, Advertising, and Marketing) to give women across communications a shared professional identity beyond labels like “marketing girlies.” The community aims to position marketing as a credible business function and build greater recognition for the strategic value of the work.

kept.heading: CREATIVE GUIDANCE ON YOUTUBE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google says creative can drive up to 49% of campaign ROI, and small creative changes can lift YouTube conversions. For Demand Gen ads, adding a human voice lifts conversions 12%, text overlays 3%, and showing the brand within the first five seconds 4%. Google recommends designing for YouTube's native look, avoiding fake buttons or oversized logos, and featuring people wherever possible.

kept.heading: HOW WE USE AI FOR EVERY ARTICLE WITHOUT MAKING AI SLOP (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Ahrefs uses AI throughout its content workflow while keeping humans responsible for judgment. Writers define the audience, angle, evidence, and original insights before using AI for research, drafting, and fact-checking. Human review gates catch weak ideas and unsupported claims before publication. Time saved on production goes toward original research and data analysis. Every article also has an owner and second reviewer who can challenge the work before it goes live.

kept.heading: GROWING LAZYWEB TO 50K+ AGENTS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Lazyweb reached 50K signups in a few months through distribution tactics built around AI agents. Removing email requirements increased activation by 50%+ and a one-line installation command added 20%. Automatic MCP routing more than doubled DAUs. Free MCP access to its blog and data-driven research also helped agents discover and use the product. Generic SEO content and novelty products had little impact. The approach focused on making Lazyweb easy for agents to use while giving away useful tools and data to drive word of mouth.

kept.heading: HELPFUL CONTENT GRADER GPT (17 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: This GPT evaluates a webpage against Google's 32-question helpful content self-assessment. Paste in a page, upload the content, or provide a URL to get started. It scores the content across quality, expertise, people-first value, and search-engine-first risks. The output includes an overall grade, section scores, evidence for each verdict, and prioritized fixes. The score is a diagnostic, not a ranking guarantee. Google's questions describe what helpful content should look like, but the score doesn't directly influence search rankings.

kept.heading: THE SHARED AGENT BRIEF: A PRACTICAL OPERATING AGREEMENT FOR GTM TEAMS (23 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI GTM workflows need clear decision rights before teams connect more tools. A Shared Agent Brief defines who contributes what, who makes each decision, what AI can handle, and when it must stop. Start with one recurring workflow and test both a normal case and a conflict case before running a small manual pilot. AI can handle research and scoring, but should pause when evidence conflicts or ownership is unclear. Expand permissions gradually, keeping external actions behind human approval.

kept.heading: WE DESIGNED FOR FACEBOOK, RIPPLE, AND MERCK. HERE'S WHAT WORKING WITH ENTERPRISE CLIENTS LOOKS LIKE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Enterprise marketing work often gets slowed down by everything around the work, not the work itself. Large companies bring more stakeholders, longer approval cycles, and conflicting feedback. The key is knowing who actually makes decisions, giving internal champions what they need to sell the work, and having one clear project owner. Once teams trust you, that relationship can expand into work across departments and years of projects.

kept.heading: DON'T LET RETAIL MEDIA TELL YOU IT'S BRAND BUILDING (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Retail media is not brand building, no matter how retailers frame it. It's the same shelf-position and end-cap money brands have paid since the 1980s, just wrapped in a modern dashboard. Retail media only reaches shoppers who are already in the store and ready to buy, not the much larger group that actually drives category growth. Treat it as a bottom-of-funnel investment that protects distribution, not a substitute for building the brand.

kept.heading: MARKETERS KNOW AI IS USING BAD DATA TO MAKE DECISIONS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 91% of marketers say data readiness is critical for AI, but only 21% say their CRM data is AI-ready.
